translations.text: When Jesus drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives: and the rest.
Christ's Passion was read just now before us, but we wish first to tell you now how he came to the city of Jerusalem and drew near to his own death, and would not avoid the Passion by flight.
"The Saviour went to the city of Jerusalem, and when he drew near to the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples, saying thus,
"Go to the town that is opposite you, and you will at once find an ass tied up, and its foal with it. Untie them and lead them to me," and so on.

It had become known to the people that a little before, the Saviour had raised Lazarus from death, who had lain stinking for four nights in the tomb. Then those who were believers came out to meet Christ with that honour, as we said before.

Some unbelievers came too, not with any honour but with great anger, as John the Evangelist said: "The chief men of the people considered among themselves that they would kill Lazarus, whom Christ had raised from death."
because many of the people believed in the Saviour through the dead man's resurrection." We will now begin the exposition of this reading.
The two disciples whom Christ sent for the ass signified the teachers whom God sent to teach mankind.
There were two of them because of what this signifies about what a teacher must have. He must have learning, so that he can teach God's people with wisdom in the right faith,
And he must set the people a good example with good works, and so with these two things, that is, with teaching and good example, always bend the lay people to God's will.
The tied ass and her foal signify two peoples, that is, the Jewish and the heathen:
I say heathen because all mankind was at that time still living in heathendom, except only the Jewish people, who kept the old law in that time.
They were tied, because all mankind was bound with sins, as the prophet said,
"Every man is bound with the ropes of his sins." Then God sent his apostles and their successors to bound mankind, and commanded them to untie them and lead them to him.
How did they untie the ass and the foal? They preached the right faith and God's commandments to the people, and also confirmed their preaching with great miracles.
Then the people turned from the devil's service to the worship of Christ, and were released from all sins through holy baptism, and led to Christ.
The ass is a stupid beast, and unclean, and more lacking in reason than other beasts, and strong for carrying burdens.
So men were, before Christ's coming, foolish and unclean, when they served idols and various sins, and bowed to the images that they themselves had made, and said to them,
"You are my God." And whatever burden the devil set on them, they bore it.
But when Christ came to mankind, he turned our foolishness to wisdom, and our uncleanness to pure conduct.
The tamed ass signified the Jewish people, who were tamed under the old law. The wild foal signified all the other people, who were still heathen and untamed;
but they became tamed and faithful when Christ sent his disciples throughout the whole world, saying thus,

"Go throughout the whole world, and teach all nations, and baptize them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit; and command them to keep all the commandments that I have taught you."
The owner of the asses asked why they were untying his asses. In the same way, the chief men of every nation wished to oppose God's preaching perversely.

But when they saw that the messengers, through God's might, healed the lame and the blind, and gave speech to the dumb, and also raised the dead to life, they could not withstand those miracles, but all together turned to God.
Christ's disciples said, "The Lord has need of the asses, and will send them back again."
They did not say "Our Lord" or "Your Lord," but simply "the Lord"; for Christ is Lord of all lords, both of men and of all creatures.
They said, "He will send them back again." We are urged and invited to God's kingdom, but we are not compelled.
When we are called, we are untied; and when we are left to our own choice, it is as if we were sent back.
It is God's mercy that we are untied; but if we live rightly, that is both God's gift and also our own diligence.
We must always pray for the Lord's help, because our own choice makes no progress unless it is furthered by the Almighty.
Christ did not order a proud steed adorned with golden trappings to be brought to him, but he chose the humble ass to carry him;
because he always taught humility, and gave the example through himself, and said thus,
"Learn from me, for I am gentle and very humble, and you will find rest for your souls."
This was prophesied about Christ, as were all the things that he did, before he was born as a man.
Zion is a mountain, and its name means 'place of watching'; and Jerusalem means 'vision of peace.'

The daughter of Zion is the congregation of believing people, who belong to the heavenly Jerusalem, in which there is always the vision of peace, without any strife; the Saviour will bring us there if we follow him.
Christ's disciples laid their garments on the ass, because he would not ride on a bare ass.
Garments signify works of righteousness, as the prophet said, "Lord, your priests are clothed with righteousness."
The naked ass is saddled with garments when the idle man is adorned for God's hand with the admonitions and examples of wise teachers; and he then carries Christ, as the apostle said,
"You are bought with a great price; therefore glorify and carry God in your body."
We carry God in our body, because we are the temple and vessel of the Holy Spirit, if we shield ourselves against foul sins; concerning this the same apostle said very terrifyingly,
"He who defiles God's temple, God will destroy him." He who is not God's temple is the devil's temple, and carries a very heavy burden on his back.
We will tell you a parable. No man can make himself king, but the people have the choice to choose as king whomever pleases them;
But after he has been consecrated as king, then he has power over the people, and they cannot shake his yoke from their necks.
so too every man has his own choice, before he sins, whether he will follow the devil's will or refuse it.
But if he binds himself with the devil's works, he cannot unbind himself by his own power, unless Almighty God unbinds him with the strong hand of his mercy.
By his own will and his own negligence he is bound, but through God's mercy he is unbound, if he afterwards earns that release from God.
The people who threw their garments under the ass's feet are the martyrs, who for faith in Christ gave their own bodies up to torments.
Some of them were burned in fire, some drowned in the sea, and killed with various tortures;
and they gave us an example that we must not, because of any persecutions or hardships, abandon our faith and turn away from Christ, any more than they did.
Many a man is counted a Christian in peacetime who would very quickly deny Christ if he were commanded what the martyrs were commanded; but his Christianity is not praiseworthy.

But that man's Christianity is praiseworthy who will not turn away from Christ for any persecution, not for sword, nor for fire, nor for water, nor for hunger, nor for bonds, but always holds his faith, with praises of God, until the end of his life.
Those who cut the branches of the trees and prepared Christ's way with them are the teachers in God's church,
who pluck the sayings of the apostles and of their successors, and with them guide God's people to faith in Christ, so that they may be ready for his coming.
The people who went before Christ, and those who followed him, all sang "Osanna Filio David," that is in our language,
"Hail to the Son of David." Those who went before Christ are the patriarchs and the prophets, who were before Christ's incarnation;
and those who went behind him are those who turned to him after Christ's birth, and turn to him daily; and they all sing one hymn of praise,
for we and they all hold one faith, as Peter the apostle said when he spoke about the patriarchs,
"We believe that we shall be saved through Christ's grace, just as they are."
They said "Son of David" because Christ, in his human nature, is of the famous royal line of David. The blessed Mary, his mother, was of that line.
They sang, "Blessed is he who comes in the name of God." The Saviour came in the name of God because the Heavenly Father sent him for our redemption;
and in all the miracles that he performed, he praised and glorified his Father's name. "Salvation be to the Son of David in the highest."
The Saviour's coming and his passion were for the salvation of both men and angels, because we increase their host, which the fallen devil diminished;
Of this the apostle Paul said, "All heavenly and earthly things were to be restored in Christ."
The Saviour remained in the temple from this day until the coming Thursday, and both by teaching and by miracles he urged the people toward truth and to right faith.
Then the chief men grew envious of his teaching, and plotted with much deliberation how they might bring him to death.

Death could not have come near him if he himself had not willed it, but he came to men because he wished to be obedient to his Father even to death, and to redeem mankind from eternal death through his temporary death.
Yet he did not compel the Jewish people to kill him; rather, the devil urged them to that deed, and God permitted it, for the redemption of all faithful mankind.
We have often said, and still say, that Christ's justice is so great that he would not take mankind from the devil by force unless the devil forfeited it.
He forfeited it when he urged the people to kill Christ, Almighty God; and then through his innocent death we were redeemed from eternal death, if we do not destroy ourselves.
Then it happened to the cruel devil as it does to the greedy fish, which sees the bait and does not see the hook that is stuck in the bait.
[?] is then greedy for the bait, and swallows the hook along with the bait. So it was with the devil: he saw the human nature in Christ, and not the divinity;
then he incited the Jewish people to kill him, and then felt the hook, Christ's divinity, by which he was choked to death and deprived of all those of mankind who believe in God.
Christ's passion did not take place on this day, but the four evangelists wrote down his passion in four accounts; one of them we read today, and the others during this week.
The Jews seized him on Friday eve and held him that night, and in the morning they fastened him to the cross with four nails and wounded him with a spear.
And then about the ninth hour, when he had died, two believing men, Joseph and Nicodemus, came and buried his body before evening in a new tomb, wrapped in costly garments.
And his body lay in the tomb on Saturday night and Sunday night; and during that time the divinity was in hell, and bound the old devil, and took Adam from him,
the first-created man, and his wife Eve, and all those of their kin who had pleased God before. Then the devil felt the hook that he had greedily swallowed.
And Christ rose from death on Easter Sunday, which is now in seven nights' time. It is more fitting to tell more about that then than now; but let us now speak about the honour of this day.
The custom stands in God's church, established by teachers, that everywhere in God's congregation the priest should bless palm branches on this day, and distribute them, so blessed, to the people;
and the servants of God must sing the hymn that the Jewish people sang to welcome Christ when he was approaching his Passion.
By this deed we imitate the faithful among the people, because they carried palm branches with a song of praise to meet the Saviour.
Now we must keep our palm until the singer begins the offertory chant, and then offer the palm to God, for the sake of what it signifies.
The palm signifies victory. Christ was victorious when he overcame the great devil and saved us:
and we too must be victorious through God's might, so that we overcome our vices, and all sins, and the devil, and adorn ourselves with good works,
and at the end of our life deliver the palm to God, that is, our victory, and thank him earnestly that, through his help, we overcame the devil, so that he could not deceive us.
The death of sinful men is evil and wretched, because they go from this short life to eternal torments;
and the death of righteous men is precious, because when they end this toilsome life, they are brought to the eternal life, and then it is as if their end were a beginning;
for they are not dead, but are turned from death to life. The body, which is the soul's garment, awaits the great judgment;
and though it be decayed to dust, God will raise it up, and bring soul and body together to the eternal life; and then Christ's promise will be fulfilled, who said thus,
"Then the righteous shall shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom," who lives and reigns forever without end in eternity. Amen.
Church customs forbid the telling of any homily on the three silent days.
